label: early copy phase (2nd-3rd output) in long sequences
explanation: Active almost only in the copy phase (96% of mass); essentially never during original input (5 of 646k steps). Concentrated on the second and third copy outputs (recall_idx 1: 52% of mass, rate 0.29; recall_idx 2: 34%), with a weak tail at the <DEL> step and recall_idx 3. Firing rate rises steadily with sequence length (L=3: 0.9% of steps, L=9: 7.6%), so it is a long-sequence, early-recall unit. Top activations peak at recall_idx 1 and decay over the next one or two steps. Within the window, the token identity changes the firing rate but no clean token rule appears: rates are higher when the next output is a digit or one of a,e,q,s,y,z (precision ~0.4-0.55) and low for i,l,p,r,c (~0.06-0.1). Adding a token filter raises precision but costs as much recall as it gains, so it is left out. Only about 36% of predicted steps actually fire, so precision is clearly incomplete. Misses are mostly short sequences (L 4-5) firing at the <DEL> step or recall_idx 0-2.
